$comment: What this repository contributes to a running stack, and what a check may
believe about it. `checked` is proved against this repository by
internal/manifest/manifest_test.go in this repository's own CI; `declared`
is a statement nobody can verify and carries its own `why`.
THREE NAMES AGAIN, AND HERE TWO OF THEM ARE PROTOCOL RATHER THAN TASTE. The
repository is `terraform-provider-taipan`; the BINARY must be called
`terraform-provider-taipan` because that is how Terraform finds a plugin;
and in a configuration it is `TAIPANBOX/taipan`, because the registry
namespace and the type name are what a user writes. engram has the same
shape for a different reason: there the third name exists because PyPI was
taken, here because the plugin protocol says so.
NOTHING IN THIS ESTATE INSTALLS IT, AND THAT IS NOT THE USUAL SENTENCE.
`runs: []` is correct: no launcher deploys a Terraform provider. TERRAFORM
installs it, from registry.terraform.io, when somebody writes
`source = "TAIPANBOX/taipan"`. So the distribution channel is a public
registry rather than any file in this estate, which is the same position
engram's `pip install engdbram` is in and the opposite of every plane, whose
installer is a launcher we own.
THE SURFACE IS FOUR RESOURCES AND ZERO DATA SOURCES, AND BOTH HALVES ARE
CHECKED. A resource is what a user's configuration names, so a resource added
in code and not here is a surface nobody declared; and `DataSources` returning
an empty slice is a fact worth pinning, because the day it stops being empty
the manifest should have to say so rather than staying quietly true.
IT READS NO ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE. Terraform passes configuration through the
provider block, not the environment, so there is nothing to declare and the
claim is checked the way qryx's and taipan's are: the reader is proved
against a planted name first.

terraform_installs_it_not_a_launcher.why: No launcher in this estate deploys a Terraform provider. Terraform fetches it from the registry when a configuration names it, which is why estate.json's `runs` is empty and right, and why the version a user gets is a published tag rather than anything a deployment pins.

the_binary_name_is_the_plugin_protocol.why: Terraform finds a plugin by that exact filename. It is not a naming choice and renaming it would break discovery, so it is recorded rather than tidied.
